Build report · 23 October 2026

PathNigeria MVP

A free career discovery platform that helps Nigerian secondary school students connect their interests to subject pathways, courses, careers and admission requirements. Schools are the paying customers; students never pay for core guidance.

The problem

Students choose subjects before they know where those subjects lead

Many students pick Science, Arts or Commercial classes without knowing which courses those choices keep open, what the courses involve, or what admission requires. PathNigeria guides them from interests to options, then to the checks they need to make.

Students · free

JSS 1 to SS 3

Explore without an account or a name. Take the quiz, browse courses and careers, print a roadmap.

Paying customer

School administrators

Principals and proprietors who run guidance programmes and see anonymous participation.

Student journey

Four steps, about 15 minutes, nothing personal collected

Screens captured from the running app at phone width (390px) in demo mode.

Tell us about you

Class, pathway, favourite subjects, activities, strengths and areas to explore. Every step can be skipped.

Take the quiz

16 questions, one at a time, with progress, Back and Skip. Each question has a “not sure” answer.

See suggestions

At least three career areas, each with “Why this was suggested” built from the student’s own answers.

Build a roadmap

Eight sections: areas, careers, courses, subjects, admissions to verify, skills, next steps and alternatives.

How suggestions work

A transparent, rule-based score that explains itself

No AI service and no hidden weighting. Every point a student earns is kept as evidence, which becomes the “why” on each result.

  1. Each quiz answer adds points to one or more of ten interest areas, such as Technology or Living things & health.
  2. Quiz score per area = points earned ÷ points possible, from 0 to 1.
  3. Onboarding choices add a gentler profile score: each subject, activity or strength adds 1 point, each chosen interest adds 2; 4 points is the maximum.
  4. Combined area score = 70% quiz + 30% profile. If the quiz was skipped, the profile score is used alone.
  5. A career area’s score is a weighted average of its linked interest areas (weights 1, 0.8, 0.6), plus 10 points if the student chose to explore it.
  6. 60 or more is a strong match, 35 or more a good match, otherwise “worth exploring”. At least three areas are always shown.
Try it: Technology & Data

This area is linked to Technology (weight 1) and Maths & logic (weight 0.8). Move the sliders to see how the score changes.

Architecture

        
One data interface, two backends

        
Pages never call the database directly. They call a small repository interface, which is backed by Supabase when keys are set and by an in-memory copy of the seed data when they aren’t.

Student pagesHome, onboarding, quiz, results, roadmap, explorers

          
Staff pagesAdmin and school dashboards, loaded on demand

Data model

        
23 tables in two versioned migrations

        
Content tables use readable IDs such as civil-engineering, so web addresses stay meaningful. Records such as enquiries use generated IDs. The seed data is written once in TypeScript and turned into supabase/seed.sql by a script.

Who can do what

        
Permissions enforced by the database, not the screen

        
Row Level Security is on for every table and all API privileges start at zero. The website only hides screens; these rules hold even if someone calls the API directly. Each row below is checked by a test that runs the real migrations on PGlite, an in-memory Postgres.

Privacy

        
Designed for minors: hold as little as possible

      

      

        

          
Whose dataWhat is keptWhere

          
            
StudentsOnboarding and quiz answers. No name, phone, birth date or location.The student’s own browser tab only. Never sent to the server.

            
Students, countedEvent type, class level and top career area. A school is attached only if the student enters a code and ticks the consent box.usage_events, with no user ID, device ID or answers.

            
School staffEmail, optional display name, role and school.Supabase Auth, profiles, school_memberships.

            
EnquiriesProfessional contact details and the message.school_enquiries, readable by platform admins only.

          
        

      

      
No advertising, no analytics service and no third-party trackers. The privacy and terms pages are drafts that need a lawyer’s review, including against the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.

    


    

      

        
Content accuracy

        
Every fact says how far it can be trusted

        
The database refuses “Verified” unless a record names its source and the date it was checked, and every status change is written to a history that can’t be edited.

      

      

        
General guidance
Plain-language explanations, such as what a course involves or which subjects commonly help.

        
Verification required
Believed typical but not yet checked for a specific institution and year. All 31 bundled admission patterns are here.

        
Verified
Checked against JAMB IBASS or the institution’s own site, with the source and date recorded. None yet.

        
Sample data
Fictional, for demonstration only, such as “Sample University (demonstration only)”.

Browser check

        
20 pages loaded in Chrome at 390px and 1366px: no console errors on any page. Two problems found and fixed: the admin table pushed the phone page sideways, and two hero labels overlapped the route line.

      

      
Not yet tested: the live Supabase path (real sign-in, saving and enquiry delivery) against an actual project. Also, twice a full test run failed every file at startup and then passed on immediate rerun; the cause wasn’t found.
